title: `lib_path()`, `cuda_path()` and `.read_components()` call `packageName()` without importing utils
description:
## Repro

```
$ R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES=NULL Rscript --vanilla -e 'cuda12.8::lib_path()'
Error in packageName() : could not find function "packageName"
Calls: <Anonymous> -> system.file
Execution halted
```

Works when `utils` is attached, fails when it isn't; e.g. `R CMD check`.

## Fix

Qualify the three direct calls in `shared/R/paths.R` and declare the
dependency: `utils::packageName()`, plus `Imports: utils` in
`shared/DESCRIPTION.template`.

Happy to submit a PR.

title: `configure` reports success after a component fails to download
description:
`shared/configure` exits 0 and prints "All components installed successfully"
when a wheel is missing or a download fails, leaving `inst/lib` empty or
partially populated.

## Cause

The component loop is the right-hand side of a pipeline, so its body runs in a
subshell:

```sh
110: tail -n +2 inst/components.tsv | while IFS="	" read -r component pypi_package version wheel_subdir extract linux_only; do
...
143:     exit 1        # "Could not find wheel for ..."
...
155:     exit 1        # "Download failed."
176: done
```

Those `exit 1`s terminate the subshell, not the script. There is no `set -e`,
and nothing inspects the pipeline's status after `done`. Execution continues
to:

```sh
222: echo "=== All components installed successfully ==="
```

which is unconditional. The RUNPATH patching in between tolerates the empty
directory quietly, because line 210 skips a glob that matched nothing:

```sh
209:     for so in inst/lib/*.so*; do
210:       [ -f "$so" ] || continue
```

Demonstration of the subshell behaviour on its own:

```
$ sh -c 'printf "a\nb\n" | while read -r x; do echo "saw $x"; exit 1; done
         echo "script continued, status=$?"
         echo "=== All components installed successfully ==="
         exit 0'
saw a
script continued, status=1
=== All components installed successfully ===
$ echo $?
0
```

`mkdir -p inst/lib` at line 107 runs before the loop, so the directory always
exists afterwards regardless of what got downloaded into it.

## Effect

The install succeeds, so R's staged installation has no reason to roll it
back. The result is a `cuda*` package that loads fine and has no libraries.
`torch:::load_cudatoolkit_libs()` then resolves `lib_path()`, finds the
directory present, lists no `.so` files, and preloads nothing without
complaint. No error, no warning, and no CUDA libraries where the user expects
them.

## Fix

The pipeline's status is already correct, as `status=1` above shows. It is
just never read:

```sh
done || exit 1
```

Verified both directions: a failing component now exits 1 before the success
banner, and a clean run still reaches it and exits 0.

Worth checking the unchecked statuses inside the loop at the same time. The
`unzip` at line 160 and `download_file` at line 151 have no status test
either, so a wheel that downloads but fails to extract takes the same silent
path.

## Provenance

Found while investigating mlverse/cudatoolkit#5. The two are independent:
#5 is an unqualified `packageName()`, this is shell control flow.
